newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ahmsa says signed $330 mln credit deal.
newsitem.headline: Ahmsa says signed $330 mln credit deal.

text.p: Mexico steel company Altos Hornos de Mexico (Ahmsa) said on Wednesday it concluded a $330 million two-tranche export-backed credit with 29 international banks.
The company said in a statement it will pay an interest rate of 8.26 percent every six months for a five-year series, and 8.46 percent for a seven-year series.
Ahmsa said the credit will be used to substitute short-term debt for long-term debt, and will be backed by export contracts with German companies Thyssen, Ferrostaal and Klockner.
"The company originally requested $150 million and the pre-subscription was three times that, to $450 million, of which Ahmsa finally accepted $330 million," the statement said.
A company official said $140 million of the credit will be used to refinance existing export-backed debt, and the other $190 million will be used to refinance dollar-denominated debt.
Ahmsa is also said to be preparing a $200 million Yankee bond. The company reported $1.5 billion in debt at the end of 1996.
